chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from Al-Muhammad from Al-Washa from Aban ibn Uthman from Abu Al-Abbas who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The one who blinds an eye of an animal, so upon him is a quarter of its price'.

key_terms.دَابَّة: animal (specifically a beast of burden or livestock)
key_terms.فَقَأَ: to blind or pierce (specifically the eye)

ai.seo_question: What is the financial compensation for blinding an animal's eye in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the principle of 'diyah al-bahim' (animal compensation) by specifying that pocking an animal's eye incurs a penalty of one-quarter of its value, reflecting the juristic view that an eye constitutes a quarter of the body's functional worth. It highlights the Shia emphasis on precise monetary restitution for property damage, distinguishing between total loss and partial impairment in Islamic civil law.

en.hubeali: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moala Bin Muhammad, from Al Washa, from Aban Bin Usman, from Abu Al Abbas who said,
‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The one who blinds an eye of an animal, so upon him is a quarter of its price’.
